newsitem.title: MEXICO: Coke FEMSA's note issue seen well received.
newsitem.headline: Coke FEMSA's note issue seen well received.

text.p: Bottler Coca-Cola FEMSA's planned issue of up to $175 million in notes due 2006 will be well-received by investors, garnering a tight spread, corporate analysts said on Thursday.
In general, Mexican corporate paper has been comfortably bought up, and Coca-Cola FEMSA stands out as a blue-chip corporate debt issuer, they added.
"It (Coca-Cola FEMSA) is a blue chip name in Mexico. Management is well-respected," said Salomon Bros corporate bond analyst Matthew B. Peck.
"It is a good name from the equity standpoint, and from a fixed-income side, so I don't think they will have too much trouble placing the issue," said Lehman Brothers beverage analyst Will Landers.
Other corporate analysts agreed, saying the spread will likely be tight.
The company said Thursday that it had filed a registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for up to $175 million in the notes due 2006.
The firm declined to further comment, saying it was in the "quiet period."
But it did say the notes will be used to replace a syndicated credit worth $165 million that is coming due in 1997.
Net proceeds will be used to repay all of its outstanding indebtedness from that credit and the remaining balance for generate corporate purposes.

Holding company Fomentos Economicos Mexicanos SA (Femsa) has an outstanding three-year $300 million bond coming due in July 1997, and analysts say they expect that will be replaced soon by another bond.
A company official told Reuters recently that they are aiming to extend the maturity on their outstanding debt.
Spreads have been dropping for Mexican borrowers recently on both bonds and commercial paper, while maturites have extended, as investors flock back to emerging markets, analysts said.
"All of Mexico has tightened significantly in the last year," said Peck.

For example, state-owned oil company Petroleos Mexicanos placed a $300 million two-year bond issue in June that yielded 190 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. This week Pemex was able to place a three-year Euro bond, priced 175 basis points over.
The narrowing of spreads on sovereign Mexican debt has led the way for tighter spreads on corporate paper and commercial loans, analysts said.
FEMSA's offering will be made by J.P. Morgan & Co, Bear Stearns & Co and Morgan Stanley & Co.
